files.skills/pr-verdict/SKILL.md: --- name: pr-verdict description: > Deliver a PR verdict on an open pull request, yours or another author's. Use only on explicit `$pr-verdict` or `/pr-verdict` invocation, or when an authorized `pr-fix` workflow composes it, including in a delegated review. Never select it for a standalone review, merge, approval, re-review, push, or PR-authoring request without explicit invocation. compatibility: > Authenticated `gh` (GitHub) or `bkt` (Bitbucket) CLI, plus an issue tracker CLI (`linear`, `gh issue create`) when a blocking defect needs a fix ticket. metadata: category: dev --- # PR Verdict ## Overview The output is a verdict that commits to a merge decision, not a list of remarks. Three properties separate it from a default agent review: every blocking finding names either a failure mechanism that breaks a claimed invariant or missing proof essential to approval, every changed observable behavior has explicit behavior-level evidence, and the limits of that evidence are declared inside the verdict. A green barrier whose gaps stay implicit is the failure this skill exists to prevent — a verdict is only as strong as what it admits it did not test. Not for re-reading your own diff before committing: perform that review and verification directly. This skill judges an open pull request and engages a decision the team will act on. That the PR is your own changes nothing about the verdict, only about how it is published — see phase 6, since GitHub refuses a request-changes review on your own PR. ## Usage Invoke `$pr-verdict ` in Codex or `/pr-verdict ` in Claude Code and Cursor. The forge is detected from `git remote get-url origin`. `pr-fix` is the sole composition entry point: a user-authorized repair permits both its initial review and its delegated reviews to invoke this skill through the host's normal skill mechanism. This permission does not authorize verdict publication or ticket creation; composed reviews stop after phase 5. Other workflows require direct user invocation. Activation is instruction-scoped, not host-enforced: the description and this usage contract limit selection. Keep model invocation available because a host-level manual-only flag also blocks the composed call; reading files manually after a rejected invocation is not the composition mechanism. After explicit invocation, typical cases are: "is this PR safe to merge?" (phase 1 checks its actual base), "review this PR before I approve it" (phase 3 turns a vague unease into a named mechanism, or drops it), "they pushed the fixes, re-review" (phase 6 finds the previous marker, sees a new SHA, and publishes a second verdict rather than editing the first). Run the six phases in order; phase 4 precedes phase 5 because a verdict without an executed barrier is an opinion. When `pr-fix` composes this skill for an initial or delegated review, stop after phase 5 and return the unpublished verdict to that workflow. This skill and its references are English; the published verdict follows the language of the PR. Publishing (phase 6) is outward-facing and visible to the team — ask for confirmation first, unless the request explicitly says to post directly. ## Steps 1. **Anchor.** Resolve the PR number, head SHA, real destination branch and checks state with `references/forges.md`, then check out that exact head. For GitHub, inspect the target branch's effective rules and relevant bypasses before describing any merge barrier; follow the enforcement procedure in that reference. A repository that has its own forge skill wins over those raw commands. If the PR is stacked on another unmerged PR, say so and make retargeting after the parent merges part of the verdict: the diff you are reading is not the diff that will land on the integration branch. A review not anchored on a named SHA is invalid, and the marker in phase 6 is what makes that anchoring visible to the next reader. When the request anticipates a PR that is not open yet, poll until it exists and anchor on it; reviewing the branch instead is a review of something the team has not proposed to merge. Before declaring readiness in phase 1, read the [integration checks](references/forges.md#integration-checks) for destination integration and barrier replay requirements. 2. **Understand before judging.** Read the PR description, the design documents it cites, and the whole diff. The attachments are part of the description: a screenshot or an uploaded log is evidence the author supplied, and the forge returns it as raw markup that a text pass slides over — download every one and look at it, in the comments too (`references/forges.md`). Restate the invariant the code claims to hold, in one sentence. Producing a blocking defect before the flow is traced end to end is forbidden: its mechanism must demonstrate the violated invariant, and you cannot name a mechanism you have not followed. In phase 2, read [commit scope](references/forges.md#commit-scope) before mapping every commit against the resolved destination to the stated PR outcome. Inventory every externally observable behavior added, removed or changed by the diff and start a changed-behavior ledger with one row per behavior. In phase 2, read [behavior evidence](references/behavior-evidence.md) for ledger, witness and user-action checks. When the aggregate PR diff changes a verification mechanism (CI routing, test oracles, caches, proof policy, or agent review rules), activate `proof-integrity-review` on the same base and exact head. This also applies when `pr-fix` composes the review. Select by the semantic change, not filenames alone; ordinary application changes and editorial-only changes do not require this audit. Complete it before phase 5, retaining its anchored evidence report with the review's evidence. Structured receipts are optional unless explicitly requested by the user or an established external workflow. Reuse relevant observed commands on the same inputs instead of running a duplicate barrier; preserve the proof auditor's fresh context and independent first pass. 3. **Sweep the failure classes.** Put every question in `references/failure-classes.md` to the diff. Record, per class, one of: not applicable, holds because ``, unproven, or broken by ``. Explain non-applicability in one clause and name the constraint, transaction, schema or executed test supporting `holds`. For unproven, name the missing evidence: block only when that proof is essential to approval under phase 5, explaining why and what would lift the gap; otherwise retain a bounded reservation. A demonstrated defect needs its named mechanism; missing proof does not establish one. When applicable, classes 11, 14 and 15 require Git-remote identity and hostile-input evidence, accounting for every selection input, and base/head measurements of performance or rewritten instructions. For class 14, check that every behavior-changing manifest, lockfile, tool configuration and pinned version is in the relevant task inputs, that file removal carries its role over to those inputs, and that a required job cannot silently pass with an empty affected-task selection on such changes. When the head under review was written in this session, delegate the review to a distinct auditor in a fresh context with no inherited conversation history, scoped to the diff. Every review requires an auditor distinct from the author in a fresh context with no inherited conversation history and an independent first analysis: withhold prior verdicts and author conclusions until that pass is recorded. Instruct the auditor not to modify the candidate and verify its state before and after. Available write tools alone do not block; technical isolation is mandatory only for an explicit security obligation. Keep unknown capabilities unknown. Reconcile the sweep with the changed-behavior ledger: the sweep can add findings, but cannot replace a row or turn absent behavior-level evidence into `holds`. 4. **Establish the barrier, then declare its holes.** Select only checks the repository already runs for affected files and consumers. Run or reuse them in the project's required environment; numbers from the wrong runner are not evidence for this head. If selection is uncertain, investigate the affected scope and existing checks, then state the uncertainty and evidence gap rather than defaulting to the complete barrier. Read the CI configuration and effective target-branch rules to identify any required merge gate; a successful CI check is advisory if no rule requires it. The relevant command is often not the package script of the same name. Report counts: builds, errors, warnings against the project's threshold, tests passed over tests run. Then enumerate what the barrier does not reach: sequential tests say nothing about a race, jsdom nothing about a browser, an in-memory database nothing about PostgreSQL, one platform nothing about the others. If nothing exercises the changed code, that absence is the review's first finding, not a reason to announce green. In phase 4, read [behavior evidence](references/behavior-evidence.md#evidence-attribution-and-reuse) before attributing evidence, reusing observations or recording description evidence. 5. **Return a verdict.** Exactly one of _changes required_, _approved with reservations_, _approved_. Complete the internal audit using `assets/verdict-template.md`, with the complete changed-behavior ledger before the blocking paragraph. Keep one row per inventoried behavior; a prose summary does not replace the rows. Both approval verdicts require every ledger row to have sufficient relevant positive evidence and required negative witnesses, with provenance and no contradictory result. Block on a demonstrated defect or essential missing evidence; explain why that proof is essential and state its lift criterion. Document other evidence limits without automatically blocking or downgrading approval. Each other blocking finding carries its named mechanism and its lift criterion — what must become true for the block to go away. Reservations cannot cover demonstrated defects, even with limited impact. Data loss or corruption blocks even when disputed. A style, naming or structure preference never blocks: label it non-blocking, or drop it. For an applicable proof-integrity audit, `PROOF_WEAK`, `PROOF_CIRCULAR`, or an absent or stale audit requires _changes required_; name the missing evidence or failing mechanism and its lift criterion. `PROOF_ADEQUATE` satisfies this additional requirement only, not the rest of the PR review. Include the proof result and observed evidence in the existing evidence gaps and behavior ledger, retaining its report as a linked review artifact. If a structured receipt was explicitly required, its missing, stale or rejected gate also blocks; absence of an optional receipt alone does not. Retain the full audit and its evidence in the review context or a local artifact; return it to `pr-fix` when composed. Use `assets/comment-template.md` for the public summary. A shorter comment never waives an audit step, ledger row, negative witness or approval prerequisite. Do not publish a separate proof verdict or interpret a path-only `NOT_APPLICABLE` as an exemption. 6. **Trace and publish.** When running inside any review pass of `pr-fix`, return the phase 5 verdict without a ticket or publication and let that workflow continue. Otherwise, open or reuse a fix ticket for blocking defects, and link the initial verdict if one exists. Never open a ticket solely to request or record a re-review: the new head-specific verdict comment is that record. Write one general comment from `assets/comment-template.md`, prefixed with the idempotency marker `` — not a rain of inline comments. Before any update or new publication in phase 6, read the [publication policy](references/forges.md#publication-policy) for identity, marker, native-state and reassessment procedures. ## Verdict policy Separate review completeness from publication length. For _approved_ with no reviewer changes or findings, publish at most eight lines: marker, verdict with short head and destination, one sentence linking decisive evidence with its actual tested candidate, and only material residual limits (at most two bullets). Omit the ledger, task counts, proof-audit codes, method narration and routine "no changes made" statements. State advisory scope once, as a verdict qualifier when applicable; do not repeat the conclusion. Do not invent limits to fill the template. For other verdicts or findings, put actionable findings and lift criteria first, followed by the relevant evidence and limits. Keep the public summary within about thirty lines; retain the full ledger internally rather than dropping audit rows to fit. Publish full audit details only when requested, still bounded and with findings first. A material limit, unresolved native review state, stacked-base requirement or actual synthetic CI candidate must remain explicit when it affects the decision; brevity cannot turn incomplete evidence into approval. `broken by` becomes a blocking defect only when its ordered failure mechanism is written out. "This looks racy" is not a mechanism; "request A snapshots at T1, request B writes at T2, A commits at T3 and B's row is absent from the successor" is. Missing proof never establishes a violated invariant; do not invent a failure mechanism or record `holds` to fit the verdict. An `unproven` class blocks only when its proof is essential under phase 5; otherwise retain a bounded reservation with its lift condition. Reservations never override the defect rule in phase 5. Classes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 12 name mechanisms that lose data, corrupt state or cross a security boundary: when broken, they block. Class 14 blocks when its demonstrated loss, wrong eligibility or routing removes required checks, prevents a promised workflow or omits a required diagnostic. An unproven diagnostic remains an evidence gap under phase 5. Classes 6, 8, 10 and 13 are usually reservations when no defect is demonstrated — promote class 6 when a concrete consumer's retry path depends on the changed code, class 8 when the degraded value reaches a person or a legal act, and class 10 when the claim is legal, evidentiary or contractual; a class 7 deferral stated with its lift condition is a reservation. Class 6 also blocks a demonstrated violation of a promised business refusal, including a named database refusal escaping as a generic server error. For class 13, label the unchanged-contract claim `unproven` until the exported bytes are compared; block when the comparison exposes a promised compatibility break or when compatibility proof is essential to approval. Missing hostile-input or output coverage in classes 11 and 12 is an evidence gap, not an invented leak: apply phase 5's essential-evidence rule and name the missing proof. For class 15, retain `unproven` until a relevant base/head comparison satisfies the declared criterion; block installation or merge when rule adoption or a required performance budget depends on it. An optional unsupported claim can instead be removed or bounded; do not invent a measured defect. Class 16 blocks when a proposed weakening defeats a required security or authorization control. Class 17 blocks when an unusable tool skips a required check or prevents a promised workflow; it also blocks installation that violates a contract to reuse an existing tool. Missing independence or usability evidence remains `unproven`; apply phase 5's essential-evidence rule rather than inventing a bypass. Class 18 blocks when stale references or missing legacy cleanup break a promised workflow or cleanup contract. Class 19 blocks a demonstrated incorrect probe conclusion; missing probe evidence follows phase 5's `unproven` rule. Class 20 blocks when following or replacing a symlink crosses the repository boundary, defeats a required file-type check or loses data or link identity. Missing symlink evidence remains `unproven`; apply phase 5's essential-evidence rule without inventing an escape or race. Class 21 blocks when undeclared or unsupported inherited state contradicts the command's independent contract and skips a required check or prevents a promised workflow; declared, supported settings are not defects. Missing evidence remains `unproven` under phase 5. Class 22 blocks demonstrated unauthorized retention, disclosure or incomplete promised erasure. Classes 23 and 24 block a demonstrated contract violation or failure of a required build, workflow or cleanup guarantee. Missing evidence follows phase 5; do not invent a leak or surviving process. Classes 25 to 27 block a demonstrated wrong result, accepted invalid reference or failing routine on existing data; missing evidence follows phase 5 without inventing a mechanism. Classes 28 to 32 block a demonstrated expiring test, broken immutability or authorized erasure, omitted legitimate source, lost reference, incorrect signature validity or source-rule violation. Missing evidence follows phase 5; do not infer a runtime failure from an unexecuted scenario. Classes are not exhaustive: apply phase 5 to defects and evidence gaps outside the catalogue too. Never downgrade a defect because no class names it; a preference never blocks. For other non-blocking findings, report at most three, one line each, or drop them. The cap is what stops the sweep from turning into a second review that competes with the verdict — rank them by whether they would change a reviewer's decision and keep the top three. If the verdict runs past about thirty lines, that is the symptom that preferences have crept into the blocking section. ## Gotchas - **The base the forge reports is not the base to review** — and it errs in both directions. A PR that targets its parent branch hides what the parent still owes; a PR that targets the integration branch while sitting on an unmerged parent includes the parent's work. Recompute the base from the parent's head and put retargeting in the lift criterion. - **The comment body passed inline** — apostrophes and backticks in a verdict break shell quoting and silently truncate the comment. Always pass the body through a file (see `references/forges.md`). - **Renaming the visible command marker** — existing comments become invisible to the duplicate guard. Keep `pr-verdict` as the stable external protocol key. - **A stale marker updated instead of superseded** — the SHA in the marker going stale on the next push is the point. Same `:` → update that comment; different SHA → publish a new verdict and leave the old one as the record of what was judged. - **A re-review ticket opened for traceability** — it duplicates the head-specific verdict and adds tracker noise without tracking a defect. Link the previous verdict, publish the new SHA marker, and reserve tickets for blocking defects. - **"Approved with reservations" used to avoid a disagreement** — that state is a claim that the consequence is bounded. If you cannot state the bound, the verdict is _changes required_. - **A missing feature reported as an omission** — an absent regulatory or business control is either a declared contract (what, why, lift condition) or a blocker. Silence is the defect, not the absence. - **The author's evidence read as absent** — a screenshot of the output comes back from the forge as an `` tag inside the body, and a text pass slides over it. The verdict then announces that nothing was observed and makes the merge conditional on steps the author has already run and attached, which reads as not having read the PR. Open every attachment in phase 2, and label supplied evidence not reproduced here as theirs. - **An unexamined green CI badge** — it does not identify the exercised checks. Inspect traceable logs and relevant inputs; reuse them with their remote provenance instead of demanding a local rerun. - **The package script mistaken for the CI gate** — the repository's `lint` script may walk the whole tree while the pipeline lints only the changed files. Its count then measures a backlog that predates the head under review, and reporting it as the barrier drowns the diff in noise. Take the command from the CI configuration, and name in the verdict which one you ran. - **A request-changes review mistaken for branch protection** — GitHub may record the review while still allowing a merge. Inspect the target branch's effective rules and bypasses, and describe the verdict as advisory without a controlled refusal. ## Constraints - Never approve without sufficient traceable barrier evidence applicable to the reviewed candidate. - Never write "everything is green": retain exact counts or non-execution in the internal audit; publish only decisive traceable evidence and material limits using `assets/comment-template.md`. - Never report a count from a command the pipeline does not run; name the gate you executed. - Never publish a blocking defect without a named failure mechanism and a lift criterion. - Never publish an essential-evidence blocker without the missing proof, why approval needs it, and a lift criterion. - Never block on style, naming or structure preference; label it non-blocking. - Never open a review that is not anchored on a head SHA. - Never approve with a demonstrated defect or essential proof missing. Require negative witnesses for modified oracles and critical guarantees, with reasoned exemptions for other behavior. - Never infer behavior-level evidence from an aggregate green barrier. - Never call a passing test a negative witness without an observed failure when the claimed behavior is broken. - Never leave a limit of the evidence implicit; the barrier's gaps belong in the verdict text. - Never report as absent, or demand in a lift criterion, evidence the PR already supplies. - Never update a verdict without confirming its exact `:` marker and publishing account; never choose arbitrarily among multiple owned matches or publish after an incomplete lookup. - Never publish two verdicts for the same `:` from the same account; update its single existing issue comment or review summary instead. - Never infer the current GitHub review state from any historical matching review; inspect the account's latest opinionated review before a native state transition. - Never sweep the failure classes on a head you wrote in this session from the context that wrote it. - Never create a ticket solely to request, schedule or record a re-review. - Never create a ticket or publish a verdict when `pr-fix` composes phases 1 through 5. - Never publish without confirmation, unless the request explicitly says to post directly. - Never claim GitHub mechanically blocks merging solely because a request-changes review was recorded. ## References - [references/forges.md](references/forges.md) — forge detection and the GitHub/Bitbucket command parity table. Read in phase 1, before the first CLI call. - [references/failure-classes.md](references/failure-classes.md) — the failure classes as questions to put to the diff. Read in phase 3. - [assets/verdict-template.md](assets/verdict-template.md) — the verdict skeleton with its required slots for the internal audit. Completed in phase 5. - [references/cases.md](references/cases.md) — behavioral cases with their expected verdicts, forge coverage, and the record of what they have never validated. - [assets/comment-template.md](assets/comment-template.md) — proportional public summaries; the complete audit stays in `assets/verdict-template.md`.

# Behavior evidence

Read during phases 2 and 4 to build the ledger and attribute and retain review evidence.

## Changed-behavior ledger

Inventory every externally observable behavior added, removed or changed by the diff. Start a
changed-behavior ledger with one row per behavior: the behavior, positive evidence on the exact
head or traceably equivalent relevant inputs, a negative witness requirement with its rationale,
and the result. Require negative witnesses for modified oracles and critical guarantees, not
systematically for every label. A witness is an executed test-first RED or a controlled faulty
variant shown to fail when the guarantee is broken. Existing witnesses are reusable when their
relevant inputs are unchanged. Keep experiments in disposable copies and verify candidate stability. A
passing regression test without an observed failing counterpart is positive evidence only; a
green aggregate count proves no individual row by itself; map its actual tests to the behavior.
Record required missing evidence as `absent`, and justified unnecessary witnesses as `not required`.

## User-action reachability

Ground each changed user action's entry point in the PR contract or added/moved control.
Ground role/stage eligibility and intentional prerequisites in an independent product,
authorization or PR contract, never the control's own guards; investigate unclear intent.
A read-only diagnosis alone does not promise an editor there. Derive valid starting states,
including empty unrelated data. Trace parent rendering, routing and enablement guards to the
usable control. API tests and tests mounting the control alone do not prove that path. Respect
declared prerequisites and verify reachability once they hold. A guard making that promised
workflow impossible is a blocker: name its location, failure sequence and a lift criterion
exercising the enclosing screen in that state.

Ship a switch with its real provider or the bootstrap the repository provides. Load the module
without a simulated provider and prove it opens in the environment where the operation must serve;
respect the policy of other environments. Report in the PR a closed default without a provider: a
test that alone injects a provider does not prove this availability.

## Evidence attribution and reuse

Then attribute each piece of evidence: measured
here, supplied by the author and not reproduced here, or absent. The three are not
interchangeable — "not observed" written over evidence sitting in the description is a false
statement about the author's work, and a lift criterion asking for a run the PR already shows
asks them to repeat themselves. What is missing in that case is a control in the repository:
name the control, not the re-run. Accept traceable CI and retained observations after checking
their artifacts and relevant source, oracle, configuration, dependency, environment and integration
inputs. Preserve original provenance and the comparison that justifies reuse; a new head need not
invalidate an unchanged mechanism's evidence. Reproduce only essential missing or invalidated
evidence. Unverifiable evidence remains unproven, not fictitiously reproduced.

## Description evidence after a push

Each description evidence entry records its tested head and integrated destination SHA, exact
command, exit status, environment and output excerpt or artifact. After each push, resolve the
final local and remote head and reconcile the description's evidence section with that revision's
actual CI run. Rerun invalidated evidence or label it historical and unproven on the new head.
Retained observations keep their original SHA; a documented relevant-input comparison permits
reuse, never relabeling an old run as executed on the current head. Required remote checks must
identify their actual tested SHA; a queue or synthetic merge candidate is a separate tree.
Preserve the forge's native merge title when a required control consumes its branch marker.

# PR forges

Read this before the first CLI call of phase 1.

## Detection

```sh
git remote get-url origin
```

- contains `github.com` → `gh`
- contains `bitbucket.org` (Cloud) or a Bitbucket Data Center host → `bkt`

**A repository's own forge skill wins over this file.** A validated wrapper encodes house PR
conventions (required reviewers, ticket prefixes, merge policy) that these raw commands do not know
about. Look for it before falling back here.

## Command parity

| Step                     | GitHub (`gh`)                                                                                                                                                                                     | Bitbucket (`bkt`)                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Metadata                 | `gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid,headRefName,headRepository,headRepositoryOwner,isCrossRepository,maintainerCanModify,baseRefName,mergeStateStatus,title,body`                                   | `bkt pr view <n> --json`                                                                                                                            |
| Head SHA                 | `.headRefOid`                                                                                                                                                                                     | Cloud `.pull_request.source.commit.hash` (12-character abbreviation), DC `.fromRef.latestCommit` — confirm the path against the actual payload      |
| Fetch the head           | `gh pr checkout <n>`                                                                                                                                                                              | `bkt pr checkout <n>`                                                                                                                               |
| CI state                 | `gh pr checks <n>`                                                                                                                                                                                | `bkt pr checks <n>`                                                                                                                                 |
| Diff                     | `gh pr diff <n>`                                                                                                                                                                                  | `bkt pr diff <n>`                                                                                                                                   |
| Existing comments        | `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n>/comments?per_page=100` and `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<n>/reviews?per_page=100`                             | `bkt pr comments <n> --json`                                                                                                                        |
| Publish                  | `gh pr comment <n> --body-file verdict.md`                                                                                                                                                        | `bkt pr comment <n> --text "$(cat verdict.md)"`                                                                                                     |
| Update                   | Issue comment: `gh api -X PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/<id> -F body=@verdict.md`; review summary: `gh api -X PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<n>/reviews/<id> -F body=@verdict.md` | Cloud: `bkt api -X PUT /2.0/repositories/{ws}/{repo}/pullrequests/<n>/comments/<id> --input "$(jq -n --rawfile b verdict.md '{content:{raw:$b}}')"` |
| Changes-requested review | `gh pr review <n> --request-changes --body-file verdict.md` — refused on your own PR; use a marker-free pointer body when updating a marked verdict without that native state on this head        | no reliable equivalent                                                                                                                              |
| Clear own change request | `gh pr review <n> --approve --body-file review-signal.md` — only after the publishing user authorizes native approval and only on another author's PR                                             | no verified Bitbucket equivalent                                                                                                                    |

`bkt` covers both Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center; the two differ on JSON shape and on some flags
(`bkt pr comments --state` is Cloud-only). Verified against `gh` 2.97 and `bkt` as installed by this
repository — re-check `--help` when a command is rejected rather than guessing a flag.

## Reading the author's evidence

The description and the comments carry attachments: a screenshot of an output, a pasted log, a
recording. The JSON body returns them as raw markup, so list the uploads and open each one.

```sh
gh pr view 1042 --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[].body)' \
  | grep -oE 'https://github\.com/user-attachments/assets/[0-9a-f-]+' | sort -u
curl -sSL -H "Authorization: token $(gh auth token)" -o attachment-1.png <url>
```

Read the downloaded file as an image. An unopened attachment is unread evidence, and phase 4 must
attribute it to the author instead of calling it absent. Verified with `gh` 2.97 against a private
repository: the token is required, and the upload answers `200 image/png`. Older bodies embed
`https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/assets/<id>` instead, which the same command reaches. The Bitbucket
attachment endpoint has not been exercised from this skill — read `bkt pr view --help` before
claiming an equivalent rather than assuming one.

## Checking out the exact head

Neither `gh pr checkout` nor `bkt pr checkout` guarantees the recorded SHA: both land on a local
branch that tracks a ref which may have moved between the metadata read and the checkout. Detach on
the SHA and prove it:

```sh
gh pr checkout 1042           # or: bkt pr checkout 1042 — brings the objects local
git checkout a1b2c3d4e5f6     # the SHA recorded in phase 1
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse a1b2c3d4e5f6)" || echo "head moved: re-anchor"
```

If the SHA is gone from the local objects, the head was force-pushed while you were reading it. Stop
and re-anchor: everything measured so far belongs to a commit nobody will merge.

Bitbucket Cloud returns only the first 12 characters of the head hash (`bkt` 0.32.1). Require the
value to be non-empty and resolve it with `git rev-parse` as above. Comparing it to
`git rev-parse HEAD` as a string rejects the right commit.

## Resolving the repair target

`pr-fix` pushes to the PR source, which is not necessarily `origin`. Parse the same metadata payload
used for the head anchor and require every source value before editing:

- GitHub: `.headRepository.nameWithOwner`, `.headRefName` and `.headRefOid`.
  `.maintainerCanModify` describes the author's fork setting, not the authenticated token's complete
  permission set; a normal push is the permission check.
- Bitbucket Cloud: `.pull_request.source.repository.full_name`,
  `.pull_request.source.branch.name` and `.pull_request.source.commit.hash`.
- Bitbucket Data Center: `.fromRef.repository.project.key`, `.fromRef.repository.slug`,
  `.fromRef.id` and `.fromRef.latestCommit`.

Validate the branch with `git check-ref-format --branch`, quote every parsed value, and obtain the
source repository's clone URL from the same forge payload or repository endpoint. Add a dedicated
temporary remote and push `HEAD` normally to that source branch. An absent value, invalid ref,
changed SHA, unavailable clone URL or rejected push stops the repair; never fall back to `origin` or
a force option.

## Finding the real base

The base the forge reports is the merge target, not the review base. Ask git what the PR actually
carries before reading a single line of diff:

```sh
git log --oneline <dest>..<head>          # every commit the merge would bring in
git diff --stat <parent-head>..<head>     # the PR's own work, when a parent PR is named
```

When the PR description names a parent PR, resolve that parent's head through the forge and diff
against it. When the two counts disagree — the forge's diff much larger than the commit range that
belongs to this author's feature — the branch is stacked and the reported diff includes the parent's
work. Say so, and require the rebase or the change of target once the parent merges.

## Pass the body through a file, never inline

A verdict contains apostrophes, backticks and accented text. Inline in a shell argument, they break
quoting or silently truncate the comment. Write `verdict.md`, then pass it:

- `gh`: `--body-file verdict.md` natively; for the API, `-F body=@verdict.md` (`-F` reads `@<path>`;
  `-f` does not).
- `bkt`: no `--body-file`. Use command substitution — `--text "$(cat verdict.md)"` in bash/zsh,
  `--text (cat verdict.md)` in fish — or build the JSON body with `jq`, which never lets the text
  reach the shell as syntax. `bkt api --input` accepts a JSON **string**, not a file or stdin marker:

```sh
bkt api -X PUT /2.0/repositories/{ws}/{repo}/pullrequests/1042/comments/1001 \
  --input "$(jq -n --rawfile b verdict.md '{content: {raw: $b}}')"
```

Data Center takes `{"text": …, "version": <n>}` instead, and rejects the update without the
comment's current `version` — read it from `bkt pr comments <n> --json` first.

## Finding a previous verdict

Build the complete first-line marker from the anchored PR number and the first 12 characters of
the anchored head SHA, for example `<!-- pr-verdict:1042:a1b2c3d4e5f6 -->`. The complete first line
must equal that marker; a prefix, another PR, another SHA or a marker later in the body is not a
match. Identify the account through the same authenticated forge context that will publish, before
reading comments. Require a nonempty stable account ID, a complete comment listing and a valid ID
for every exact match. A failed API call, malformed listing or missing author ID on an exact match
stops publication, even if another owned match is present. Do not turn an uncertain read into an
empty result.

For GitHub, `gh api user --jq .id` identifies the publishing account. Read **both** paginated
collections; `gh pr review --request-changes` creates a review summary, which is not an issue
comment. The REST objects expose `.user.id`, `.body` and `.id`; review summaries also expose
`.state` and `.commit_id`. Use the same repository and PR established in phase 1:

```sh
gh api user --jq '.id'
gh api --paginate --slurp 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/1042/comments?per_page=100' |
  jq --arg marker '<!-- pr-verdict:1042:a1b2c3d4e5f6 -->' \
    'if length > 0 and all(.[]; type == "array") and
        all(.[][]; type == "object" and (.body | type == "string") and (.id | type == "number")) then
       [.[][] | select((.body // "" | split("\n")[0]) == $marker) | {id, author_id: .user.id}]
     else error("invalid issue-comment listing") end'
gh api --paginate --slurp 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/1042/reviews?per_page=100' |
  jq --arg marker '<!-- pr-verdict:1042:a1b2c3d4e5f6 -->' \
    'if length > 0 and all(.[]; type == "array") and
        all(.[][]; type == "object" and (.body | type == "string") and (.id | type == "number")) then
       [.[][] | select((.body // "" | split("\n")[0]) == $marker) | {id, author_id: .user.id, state, commit_id}]
     else error("invalid review listing") end'
```

Configure bash or zsh to propagate a failed pipeline stage so a failed paginated fetch cannot look
like an empty list. Compare the numeric `author_id` with the numeric viewer ID, and keep the source
(`issue comment` or `review summary`) with each match. A GitHub login name or
`author_association` is not the ownership key. Immediately before an update, read the selected
object again by ID and recheck its author and exact first-line marker. Update a review summary with
the review endpoint in the command table; updating an issue comment through that endpoint fails.
The review update changes its body, not its native review state. Use the **full**, chronological
GitHub review listing, not only the marker-filtered matches, to find the publishing account's last
opinionated review (`APPROVED` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED`) and its `commit_id`. Ignore later `COMMENTED`
reviews when deciding the opinionated state. If review state is dismissed or cannot be established,
stop before publishing a conflicting verdict. GitHub's REST references document
[issue comments](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments) and
[review summaries](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews) as separate resources.

```sh
publisher_id=$(gh api user --jq '.id')
gh api --paginate --slurp 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/1042/reviews?per_page=100' |
  jq --arg publisher_id "$publisher_id" '
    def known_state:
      . == "APPROVED" or . == "CHANGES_REQUESTED" or . == "COMMENTED" or
      . == "PENDING" or . == "DISMISSED";
    def valid_account_review:
      (.id | type == "number") and (.state | known_state) and
      (if .state == "APPROVED" or .state == "CHANGES_REQUESTED" then
         (.commit_id | type == "string") and (.commit_id | length > 0)
       else true end);
    if length > 0 and all(.[]; type == "array") and
       all(.[][]; type == "object") and
       all(.[][] | select((.user.id | @json) == $publisher_id); valid_account_review) then
      [.[][] | select((.user.id | @json) == $publisher_id)
       | select(.state == "APPROVED" or .state == "CHANGES_REQUESTED" or .state == "DISMISSED")
       | {id, state, commit_id}] | last
    else error("invalid review listing") end'
```

GitHub documents chronological review listing. A `null` result means this account has no
opinionated review. Validate the numeric viewer ID before running this query; an uncertain or
dismissed state stops the transition.

For a blocking reassessment of someone else's PR, skip another request-changes review only when
that last opinionated review is `CHANGES_REQUESTED` **and** its `commit_id` is the anchored head.
Otherwise submit a marker-free request-changes review linking the updated marked verdict, then
verify that the publishing account's latest opinionated review on this head is
`CHANGES_REQUESTED`. A historical change request followed by an approval does not satisfy this
check. For a new head, the newly created marked request-changes review itself establishes the
state.

For an approval verdict on someone else's PR, check whether the latest opinionated review by this
account is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, even when it belongs to an older head. If so, native approval is
needed to clear the existing request. Name that action when asking to publish; if it is not
authorized, return the verdict unpublished instead of announcing approval over an active native
block. Use a pending marked body first: keep any earlier assessment intact and add a visible line
saying the new approval assessment awaits native approval and is not yet published. On a new head,
create a marked pending comment containing that status. Reconcile the pending object's author,
marker and URL before the next write. Submit one marker-free `gh pr review --approve` review whose
body links to that object, then verify through a fresh review listing that this account's latest
opinionated review is `APPROVED`. Only then replace the pending body with the complete approved
`verdict.md` and read it back. If native approval fails or is uncertain, do not write the final body;
re-read the reviews and pending object, then report only their observed states. If the final body
update fails or is uncertain, re-read the object by ID: a confirmed final body completes the
publication, a confirmed pending body leaves it incomplete, and an unreadable body leaves its state
unknown. Stop and reconcile before retrying; never repeat a native approval already observed.
If no active change request exists, retain the existing comment-only approval publication. Never
put the verdict marker in a state-only review. A state review does not by itself prove a mechanical
merge block or unblock; branch rules and bypasses still matter.

For Bitbucket Cloud, `bkt api /2.0/user` returns the publishing account's `.uuid`.
`bkt pr comments 1042 --json` returns all comments in `.comments` (`null` when empty), including
inline comments and replies. Match the exact first line of `.content.raw` and compare `.user.uuid`
with the authenticated UUID; do not use display names. Exclude a deleted comment from updates.
Only a top-level global comment, with both `.parent` and `.inline` absent, is eligible for update.
An exact marker in an owned reply or inline comment is misplaced: stop rather than updating it or
publishing another verdict. An unknown author on such a match also stops; a known foreign reply or
inline comment does not mask publication by the current account.
`bkt` 0.34.0 follows Cloud pagination; a CLI or API failure stops publication. Check that
`.comments` is an array or `null`, then read the selected comment through
`bkt api /2.0/repositories/{ws}/{repo}/pullrequests/1042/comments/<id>` and verify its author and
marker before using the Cloud update endpoint in the command table.
The Cloud API documents `.user`, `.content.raw`, `.deleted` and the update endpoint. If a live
payload omits `.user.uuid`, `.content.raw` or `.id`, stop and inspect the actual response.
The [Cloud user API](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-users/)
identifies the current account; the [pull request comments API](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-pullrequests/)
defines the comment data and update operation.

```sh
bkt api /2.0/user --json --jq '.uuid'
bkt pr comments 1042 --json |
  jq --arg marker '<!-- pr-verdict:1042:a1b2c3d4e5f6 -->' \
    'if has("comments") and (.comments == null or (.comments | type == "array")) and
        all((.comments // [])[]; type == "object" and (.id | type == "number") and
            (.deleted == true or (.content.raw | type == "string"))) then
       [(.comments // [])[] | select(.deleted != true)
        | select((.content.raw // "" | split("\n")[0]) == $marker)
        | {id, author_uuid: .user.uuid, general: (.parent == null and .inline == null)}]
     else error("invalid Bitbucket comment listing") end'
```

Bitbucket Data Center comments use `.author` and `.text`, but its documented user listing does not
identify which account owns the current token. A configured `bkt` username alone is not forge
proof of the publishing account. Until a verified authenticated-user response is available for the
target instance, stop before creating or updating a Data Center verdict. Do not infer ownership from
a matching marker or a display name.

Classify all exact, not-deleted matches across the applicable surfaces before writing:

| Result                                                                           | Action                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One eligible owned match                                                         | Re-read it, then update that object through its own endpoint.                     |
| No owned match, only known foreign matches or none                               | Publish a new verdict for the current account. Foreign comments remain untouched. |
| More than one owned match                                                        | Stop and report their IDs; never choose one or add another.                       |
| Owned match in an ineligible Bitbucket reply or inline comment                   | Stop and report its ID; never update it as the general verdict.                   |
| Unknown author, missing ID, incomplete listing or uncertain publication response | Stop and reconcile through a fresh remote read before retrying.                   |

After an update, read back its returned ID and verify the author and marker. Creation commands may
return only a URL or success message, so repeat the full lookup after creation and require exactly
one newly owned match on the current marker before treating publication as confirmed. On a timeout
or uncertain response, do the same remote reconciliation before any retry; if it remains uncertain,
stop without another write. Same `<pr>:<sha>` is account-local idempotency; a different SHA receives a new verdict and leaves the old
record intact. Do not use `gh pr comment --edit-last`: the last comment may carry another marker.
The lookup and re-read do not lock the forge: simultaneous publishers can both create a comment.
Coordinate concurrent publication for the same account and head, and report any duplicate found by
post-publication reconciliation rather than choosing one to overwrite.

## Review state and merge enforcement

GitHub records `gh pr review --request-changes` as a review state. Its [review documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/review-pull-requests/approving-a-pull-request-with-required-reviews)
says this state is informational unless an applicable ruleset or classic branch protection requires
pull requests; reviewer permissions and bypass rights also matter. Inspect the actual destination
branch, not the local checkout or the repository default. Substitute the target repository and
URL-encoded destination branch from the phase-1 anchor; `{branch}` in `gh api` would resolve to the
current checkout branch:

```sh
gh api "repos/$target_repository/branches/$encoded_destination_branch" --jq '{name, protected}'
gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$target_repository/rules/branches/$encoded_destination_branch"
gh api "repos/$target_repository/branches/$encoded_destination_branch/protection"
```

The branch rules endpoint reports [active rulesets applicable to that branch](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules#get-rules-for-a-branch),
including rules from higher scopes. Its slurped response contains one array per page; inspect every
page before concluding that no pull-request rule applies. The classic protection endpoint returns
`Branch not protected` when no classic rule exists; that response alone says nothing about rulesets.
Read the applicable pull-request requirement, the reviewer's `write` or stronger permission, and
any administrator or ruleset bypass for the account that would merge. Inspect the ruleset details
when bypass actors matter; [GitHub may omit them without ruleset write access](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules#get-a-repository-ruleset).
Treat a failed or incomplete lookup as unknown, not as proof of no protection.

If no active rule demonstrates a block, or a bypass or permission remains uncertain, label the
verdict advisory even when GitHub records `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Claim a mechanical block only after a
controlled PR with the same repository, destination branch, applicable rules, reviewer permission
and merge account actually refuses merging because of that review. Record the repository, branch,
active rules, account and observed refusal in the verdict. A rule listing or disabled merge button
caused by another condition is not that observation. Do not create or merge a controlled PR solely
to support an ordinary verdict; use the advisory wording when the evidence is unavailable.

Bitbucket [Cloud](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/announcement-new-request-changes-webhooks/)
and [Data Center](https://confluence.atlassian.com/bitbucketserver/review-and-discuss-a-pull-request-808488540.html)
have a Request changes reviewer status,
but this skill has no verified `bkt` command to set it. `bkt pr approve` exists; declining a PR is a
different act with a different meaning. Here the comment **is** the verdict, and the closing
sentence ("do not approve or merge this head") remains an advisory request.

GitHub falls back to a comment-only verdict whenever the authenticated account authored the
PR: it rejects the call with `Can not request changes on your own pull request`, and there is no
flag around it. `gh pr view --json` exposes no `viewerDidAuthor` field (checked on `gh` 2.97), so
compare the author against the token yourself, in phase 1 —

```sh
test "$(gh pr view 1042 --json author --jq .author.login)" = "$(gh api user --jq .login)" &&
  echo "own PR: request-changes review unavailable"
```

When it is your own PR, publish the comment alone and state its advisory scope. In every GitHub
case, separate the recorded review state from demonstrated merge enforcement.

## Publication policy

Apply the
[identity, exact-marker and ambiguity procedure](#finding-a-previous-verdict) before any update or
new publication. GitHub issue comments and review summaries are separate lookup and update
surfaces. Update only the single matching verdict owned by the publishing account; a foreign
match does not prevent that account from publishing its own. Stop on an unknown author, multiple
owned matches or an incomplete lookup. A different SHA gets a new verdict and leaves the old one
intact. Re-read before publishing using `assets/comment-template.md`: an uncomplicated approval
stays within eight lines; other summaries stay within about thirty. Keep the complete required
behavior ledger in the internal audit, not in the public summary unless details were requested. On
GitHub, _changes required_ establishes `CHANGES_REQUESTED` through
`gh pr review --request-changes` on another author's PR. On an updated marked verdict, compare
the account's latest opinionated review and its SHA before deciding whether another native
review is needed. If a later approval verdict must clear this account's earlier change request,
name the native approval in the publication confirmation and submit it only with that
authorization. Keep state-only reviews marker-free and link the marked verdict, as specified under
[finding a previous verdict](#finding-a-previous-verdict).
GitHub refuses a request-changes review on your own PR, and this skill has no verified `bkt`
command for the analogous Bitbucket state. A recorded request for changes does not by itself
establish a mechanical merge block.
State the advisory scope in the verdict unless the GitHub procedure has demonstrated an actual
refusal for the applicable rules and account. For your own GitHub PR or Bitbucket, publish the
comment alone and state its advisory scope.
A same-head reassessment under changed policy or new evidence is a new dated assessment with
its policy and evidence references. Preserve the earlier verdict and append the reassessment
inside the existing marked comment; never replace a historical rejection with an approval.

## Integration checks

Fetch the resolved destination and record its SHA. Run `git merge-tree --write-tree` with that
ref and the head; absence of textual conflicts does not prove integration compatibility. Before
declaring readiness, require the current destination to be integrated into the candidate and
replay the relevant barrier on that tree. A read-only review does not authorize updating the
source branch: report the required integration instead. Search the integrated tree for every
consumer of a new mandatory contract, including consumers added on the destination; after
conflict resolution, rerun the controls whose rejected behavior could have been restored.

## Commit scope

Inspect every commit against the resolved destination and map it to the stated PR outcome.
Unrelated changes must be removed under development authority or explicitly disclosed in the
description. Verification tooling accompanying functional changes, including a correction to a
test oracle or a preflight, needs a separate PR or an explicit coupling rationale. Coherent
subtasks may share a PR. Flag temporary `wip` subjects and violations of the repository's commit
convention before publication or an update.
